newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Samsung adjusts share buying offer price.
newsitem.headline: Samsung adjusts share buying offer price.

text.p: South Korea's Samsung Electronics Co Ltd said on Monday it had adjusted offer prices to buy its shares from shareholders opposing the company's plan to absorb its unlisted subsidiary, Kwangju Electronics Co.
Samsung will now pay 64,250 won per common share, not 64,330 won as earlier announced, and 31,749 won per preferred share, instead of 31,711 won.
The offer is valid for 20 days after a shareholders' meeting scheduled for February 28 for a formal approval of the merger.
Samsung has agreed to absorb Kwangju Electronics as of July 1, 1997.
Following the announcement of the merger plan earlier on Monday, the Korea Stock Exchange halted trading in shares of Samsung Electronics. The shares will resume trading on Tuesday.
Samsung common shares last traded at 60,100 won, down 200, and its preferred shares at 29,900, down 600.
